prompt: Leave every existing C# business logic file unchanged. Using {TECH}, integrate every public method so the page shows each result. Follow the project rules. Do not run any commands, installs, or builds. Only write files.

rules.source:
---
description: REST endpoints and typed fetch
alwaysApply: true
---

Turn the backend into an ASP.NET Core web app. Do not edit the existing business logic files.

Expose every public method as its own HTTP endpoint. Give each method its own request type and its own response type. Each argument is a property. The response is an object, not a bare number or boolean. Do not reuse a type for two methods.

Put one C# type in each file, and name the file after the type.

In `src/api.js`, one async function per method. Each calls `fetch`, checks `response.ok`, and returns the JSON. `App.jsx` calls each function and shows the result.

Do not run commands.

---
description: Graftcode direct calls
alwaysApply: true
---

Read the public methods in the C# files. Do not edit those files.

In `src/App.jsx`, import `GraftConfig` and the classes from `@graft/nuget-energypriceservice`. Set `GraftConfig.host = 'ws://localhost:80/ws'`. Call every public method once with literal numbers. A JavaScript name is the C# name with a lowercase first letter. Append each result to `pre#out`. No forms and no other components.

The generated client uses top-level await. In `vite.config.js`, set `build.target` to `esnext`.

Write `backend/Dockerfile`. Build and publish with the .NET 8 SDK. The runtime image is `graftcode/netcore:10.0`. Copy the published output to `/usr/app`, expose port 80, and start `gg --runtime netcore --modules /usr/app/EnergyPriceService.dll --port 80`.

Do not run commands. Do not add controllers, routes, DTOs, or fetch.
